title: Bekhorot 38
description: The skull-deficiency debate ends with Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh’s testimony on vessels without a receptacle and the size of a drilled hole, and the mishna turns to blemishes of the eye: the eyelid, cataracts, the tevallul, and pale spots and tears that are constant.
topics: 🕳️ “A drilled hole and its obstruction”: Beit Shammai’s measure for a deficient skull
🏺 Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh: a vessel with no receptacle has no distinct outside
💧 Impurity of liquids, a rabbinic decree, and the indicator that saves teruma from burning
🪙 A large drill, a small drill of doctors, and a sela of Nero
👁️ Blemishes of the eye: the eyelid, a cataract, the snail, the snake and the berry
🧵 The tevallul: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei on “no blemishes in the white”
🧓 An elder of the neighborhood: a person may not examine his own firstborn, but may teach his students
🌾 Constant tears: testing with moist and then dry fodder, in Adar and Nisan, Elul and Tishrei

a1.he: כִּמְלֹא נֶקֶב שֶׁל עוֹל! אִישְׁתִּיק, וְאָמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: שֶׁמָּא מַקְדֵּחַ וְחִיסּוּמוֹ שָׁנִינוּ.

a2.he: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב תַּחְלִיפָא: לָא תֵּימָא שֶׁמָּא, אֶלָּא וַדַּאי מַקְדֵּחַ וְחִיסּוּמוֹ, צָרִיךְ לְהִתָּלוֹת עָלֶיהָ כְּחִזְקִיָּה אֲבִי עִקֵּשׁ.

a3.he: דִּתְנַן: זוֹ עֵדוּת הֵעִיד חִזְקִיָּה אֲבִי עִקֵּשׁ לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּיַבְנֶה, שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס — אֵין לוֹ אֲחוֹרַיִם לַחֲלִיקָה. נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ, נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ — נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ.

a4.he: כְּלִי חֶרֶס, בְּתוֹכוֹ תְּלָה רַחֲמָנָא — אִית לֵיהּ תּוֹךְ — אִיטַּמִּי לֵיהּ, לֵית לֵיהּ תּוֹךְ — לָא אִיטַּמִּי לֵיהּ!

a5.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין: הָכִי קָאָמַר, כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס — כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בִּכְלִי שֶׁטֶף אֵין לוֹ אֲחוֹרַיִם לַחֲלִיקָה, נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ, נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ — נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ.

a6.he: לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְלְיֵיהּ בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס? נֵימָא: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי שֶׁטֶף — אֵין לוֹ אֲחוֹרַיִם לַחֲלִיקָה!

a7.he: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ תּוֹךְ — הֲרֵי הוּא כִּכְלִי חֶרֶס; מָה כְּלִי חֶרֶס, נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ, לֹא נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — לֹא נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ; אַף כְּלִי שֶׁטֶף, נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ, לֹא נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — לֹא נִטְמָא גַּבּוֹ.

a8.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּלִי חֶרֶס, גַּלִּי בֵּיהּ רַחֲמָנָא ״תּוֹכוֹ״, אֶלָּא כְּלִי שֶׁטֶף, מִי גַּלִּי בֵּיהּ רַחֲמָנָא תּוֹכוֹ?

a9.he: אִי בְּטוּמְאָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא — הָכִי נָמֵי, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? בְּטוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין דְּרַבָּנַן, דִּתְנַן: כְּלִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא אֲחוֹרָיו בְּמַשְׁקִין — אֲחוֹרָיו טְמֵאִין, תּוֹכוֹ אׇגְנוֹ אׇזְנוֹ וְיָדָיו טְהוֹרִין, נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ — כּוּלּוֹ טָמֵא.

a10.he: מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, אֵין אוֹכֶל מְטַמֵּא כְּלִי, וְאֵין מַשְׁקֶה מְטַמֵּא כְּלִי, וְרַבָּנַן הוּא דִּגְזוּר מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקֵה זָב וְזָבָה.

a11.he: הִלְכָּךְ, שַׁוְּיוּהּ רַבָּנַן כְּטוּמְאָה דִּכְלִי חֶרֶס, וְלָא שַׁוְּיוּהּ רַבָּנַן כְּטוּמְאָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא דְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ.

a12.he: עֲבַדוּ רַבָּנַן הֶיכֵּירָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לִישְׂרוֹף עֲלֵיהּ תְּרוּמָה וְקָדָשִׁים. אִי הָכִי, אֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ נָמֵי, לֶיעְבֵּיד נָמֵי הֶיכֵּירָא!

a13.he: כֵּיוָן דַּעֲבַדוּ הֶיכֵּירָא בְּיֵשׁ לוֹ תּוֹךְ, יְדִיעַ דְּאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ דְּרַבָּנַן.

a14.he: וְאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ בִּכְלִי שֶׁטֶף, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בַּר קַבּוֹלֵי טוּמְאָה הוּא? דּוּמְיָא דְּשַׂק בָּעֵינַן, מָה שַׂק מִיטַּלְטֵל מָלֵא וְרֵיקָן, אַף כֹּל מִיטַּלְטֵל מָלֵא וְרֵיקָן.

a15.he: בְּהָנָךְ דַּחֲזוּ לְמִדְרָסוֹת. אִי הָכִי, חֶרֶס נָמֵי! אֵין מִדְרָס בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס.

a16.he: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַקְדֵּחַ גָּדוֹל שָׁנִינוּ.

a17.he: מִכְּלָל דְּמַקְדֵּחַ סְתָם זוּטַרא נָמֵי מִכְּסֶלַע. הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?

a18.he: דִּתְנַן: בְּאֵיזֶה מַקְדֵּחַ אָמְרוּ? בְּקָטָן שֶׁל רוֹפְאִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בְּגָדוֹל שֶׁל לִשְׁכָּה.

a19.he: וּלְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, מִי נִיחָא? הָוֵה לֵיהּ מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל. וַאֲנַן דִּתְנַן — תְּנַן, דְּלָא תְּנַן — לָא תְּנַן!

a20.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: סֶלַע נִירוֹנִית שָׁנִינוּ, כְּמַקְדֵּחַ גָּדוֹל, סֶלַע סְתָם זוּטַרא מִמַּקְדֵּחַ סְתָם.

a21.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָרִיס שֶׁל עַיִן שֶׁנִּיקַּב, שֶׁנִּפְגַּם, שֶׁנִּסְדַּק, הֲרֵי בְּעֵינוֹ דַּק, תְּבַלּוּל, חִלָּזוֹן, נָחָשׁ, עָצָב. אֵיזֶהוּ תְּבַלּוּל? לָבָן הַפּוֹסֵק בַּסִּירָא וְנִכְנָס בַּשָּׁחוֹר. שָׁחוֹר נִכְנַס בַּלָּבָן — אֵינוֹ מוּם.

b1.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי הָרִיס? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תּוֹרָא בָּרָא דְּעֵינָא. דַּק תְּבַלּוּל, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דַּק מְשׁוּקָּע — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, צָף — אֵינוֹ מוּם.

b2.he: וְהָתַנְיָא אִיפְּכָא! לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בַּשָּׁחוֹר הָא בַּלָּבָן. וְהָא: אֵין מוּמִין בַּלָּבָן! אֶלָּא, הָא בְּדוּק לָבָן, הָא בְּדוּק שָׁחוֹר.

b3.he: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: סָח לִי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא: דַּק שָׁחוֹר מְשׁוּקָּע — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, צָף — אֵינוֹ מוּם. דַּק לָבָן מְשׁוּקָּע — אֵינוֹ מוּם, צָף — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, וְסִימָנָיךְ: בַּרְקָא.

b4.he: חִלָּזוֹן נָחָשׁ וְעָצָב. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: חִלָּזוֹן הוּא נָחָשׁ, אוֹ דִלְמָא חִלָּזוֹן אוֹ נָחָשׁ?

b5.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: סָח לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר, זָקֵן אֶחָד הָיָה בִּשְׁכוּנָתֵינוּ, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי לָקוֹנְיָא שְׁמוֹ, וּמִיָּמַי לֹא עָבַרְתִּי לְפָנָיו. פַּעַם אַחַת עָבַרְתִּי לְפָנָיו, אָמַר לִי: שֵׁב בְּנִי, שֵׁב. חִלָּזוֹן זֶה מוּם קָבוּעַ לִשְׁחוֹט עָלָיו, וְזֶהוּ נָחָשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים.

b6.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ: אֵין אָדָם רוֹאֶה מוּמִין לְעַצְמוֹ, אֲבָל מוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה לַתַּלְמִידִים, וְתַלְמִידִים מוֹרִין לוֹ.

b7.he: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁמּוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה וּבָא, אִם קוֹדֶם מַעֲשֶׂה אֲמָרָהּ — שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ, וְאִם לָאו — אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ! אִיהוּ נָמֵי מוֹרֶה וּבָא הֲוָה מֵעִיקָּרָא.

b8.he: אֵיזֶהוּ תְּבַלּוּל? לָבָן הַפּוֹסֵק אֶת הַסִּירָא. מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: לָבָן וְנִכְנָס בַּשָּׁחוֹר, שָׁחוֹר וְנִכְנָס בַּלָּבָן — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לָבָן וְנִכְנָס בַּשָּׁחוֹר — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, שָׁחוֹר וְנִכְנָס בַּלָּבָן — אֵינוֹ מוּם, שֶׁאֵין מוּמִין בַּלָּבָן.

b9.he: אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי? דִּכְתִיב: ״יָצָא מֵחֵלֶב עֵינֵימוֹ״, תַּרְבָּא דְּעֵינָא — אִיקְּרִי, ״עֵינֵימוֹ״ סְתָמָא — לָא אִיקְּרִי. וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ? מָה לְשׁוֹן ״תְּבַלּוּל״? דָּבָר הַמְבַלְבֵּל אֶת הָעֵינַיִם.

b10.he: מַתְנִי׳ חֲוַרְוָור וְהַמַּיִם הַקְּבוּעִין. אֵיזֶהוּ חֲוַרְוָור הַקָּבוּעַ? כֹּל שֶׁשָּׁהָה שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם. רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אֹמֵר: בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם.

b11.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מַיִם הַקְּבוּעִין: אָכַל לַח וְיָבֵשׁ שֶׁל גְּשָׁמִים, לַח וְיָבֵשׁ שֶׁל שְׁלָחִים, אוֹ אָכַל הַיָּבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַלַּח — אֵינוֹ מוּם, עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל הַלַּח וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַיָּבֵשׁ.

b12.he: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: חֲוַרְוָור קָבוּעַ — אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, וּמַיִם הַקְּבוּעִים — שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חֲוַרְוָור — שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם.

b13.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מַיִם הַקְּבוּעִים: אָכַל לַח וְיָבֵשׁ שֶׁל בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין, אוֹ שֶׁאָכַל יָבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָכַל הַלַּח — אֵין מוּם עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל יָבֵשׁ אַחַר הַלַּח, וְיֶשְׁנוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים.

b14.he: וְהָא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ תְּנַנְהִי: אָכַל לַח וְיָבֵשׁ שֶׁל גְּשָׁמִים, לַח וְיָבֵשׁ שֶׁל בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין!

b15.he: חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: אָכַל לַח וְיָבֵשׁ שֶׁל גְּשָׁמִים — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם, בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין — אֵינוֹ מוּם, וְהַגְּשָׁמִים נָמֵי, אָכַל יָבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָכַל לַח — אֵינוֹ מוּם, עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל יָבֵשׁ אַחַר הַלַּח.

b16.he: וְיֶשְׁנוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים. אִינִי? וְהָתַנְיָא — וְהָא רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָאן: אֲדָר וְנִיסָן — לַח, אֱלוּל וְתִשְׁרִי — יָבֵשׁ! אֵימָא: אֲדָר וַחֲצִי נִיסָן — לַח, אֱלוּל וַחֲצִי תִשְׁרֵי — יָבֵשׁ.

b17.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לַח בִּזְמַן לַח, וְיָבֵשׁ בִּזְמַן הַיָּבֵשׁ, אוֹ דִלְמָא: לַח וְיָבֵשׁ בִּזְמַן הַלַּח?

b18.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָאן: אֲדָר וְנִיסָן — לַח, אֱלוּל וְתִשְׁרִי — יָבֵשׁ. דִּלְמָא פֵּירֵי דֶּאֱלוּל וְתִשְׁרִי מַאֲכִילִנַן לֵיהּ בַּאֲדָר וְנִיסָן!

b19.he: וְכַמָּה מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן עָרוֹבָא: כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת. אָמַר רָבָא: (בָּעֵי) [בָּעַן] בְּמַעְרְבָא: כִּגְרוֹגְרוֹת בִּסְעוּדָה רִאשׁוֹנָה,

messages.text: Continued from 37b: Rav Ḥisda objected to Rav Taḥlifa that if Beit Hillel’s measure for a deficient skull is a sela, it is the same as Beit Shammai’s “drilled hole”, since a mishna rules that a window made by a person transmits impurity at the size of the large drill of the Temple chamber, which is like a sela of Nero, “and its size is…”
like the size of the hole of a yoke of an animal.

Evidently, the measure of the drilled hole stipulated by Beit Shammai with regard to a deficient skull equals the size of a sela coin stipulated by Beit Hillel according to the statement of Rav Taḥlifa.

notes.he: שעושין בו נקב ותוקעין בו יתד לקשור רצועות העול אלמא מקדח הוי כסלע ומאי איכא בין ב"ש ובין ב"ה:
notes.en: Like the size of the hole of a yoke: in which they make a hole and insert a peg to tie the straps of the yoke. Evidently a drilled hole is like a sela; so what difference is there between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel?

messages.text: Rav Taḥlifa was silent.

notes.he: רב תחליפא:
notes.en: He was silent: Rav Taḥlifa.

notes.en: He was silent: Rav Taḥlifa.

messages.text: @Rav Taḥlifa bar Avudimi Perhaps we learned that Beit Shammai did not mean the size of a drilled hole alone, but rather the size of a drilled hole and its obstruction, i.e., a hole that allows for the drill to be inserted and removed. This is slightly larger than the sela mentioned by Beit Hillel.

notes.he: דקאמר ב"ש בגולגולת מקדח וחיסומו שנינו דלאחר שנעשה החור מצדדין את המקדח ונוטל מצידי הנקב ומרחיבין את הנקב כדי שיכנס מקדח ויוצא בריוח והיינו חיסום שנוטל מה שחיסם וסותם את הנקב ואינו מניח ליכנס המקדח ברוחב ומקדח וחיסומו הוי יותר מסלע:
notes.en: And Rav Ḥisda said to him: Perhaps the drill that Beit Shammai speak of regarding the skull is “a drill and its ḥisum” that we learned. For after the hole is made, they turn the drill to the sides, take from the sides of the hole and widen it, so that the drill can enter and exit with room to spare. That is ḥisum: one removes what obstructs [ḥisem] and blocks the hole and does not let the drill enter with its full width. And a drill with its ḥisum is more than a sela.

notes.dh: בתר הכי אמר שמא האי כמלא מקדח גדול דקתני הכא דהוי סלע במקדח וחיסומו שנינו
notes.he: באותו מקדח שנוקבין בו את החביות שהוא דק מלמטה ועב מלמעלה שאותו עב סותם את הנקב והיינו וחיסומו והיינו כמלא מקדח נכנס ויוצא ותפשוט מיהא דבעיא דרבי אושעיא ואותו כמלא מקדח דב"ש דגלגלת דזוטר הוי מכסלע. וב"ה אמרי כדי שינטל מן החי היינו כסלע והכי איכא בינייהו:
notes.en: Afterward he said: Perhaps this “size of a large drill” taught here, which is a sela, is “a drill and its ḥisum” that we learned: that drill with which they bore jugs, which is thin below and thick above, and that thick part blocks the hole; that is “and its ḥisum,” and that is “the size of a drill,” entering and exiting. And at any rate resolve from this the dilemma of Rabbi Oshaya [Rav Hoshaya’s question on 37b]. And Beit Shammai’s “size of a drill” regarding a skull is smaller than a sela, while Beit Hillel say “enough that if removed from a living person [he would die],” which is a sela; and this is the difference between them.

messages.text: @Rav Ḥisda Do not say: Perhaps. Rather, say: Beit Shammai definitely was referring to the size of a drilled hole and its obstruction, and you can rely on this explanation since it is certainly correct, as certain as the testimony of Ḥizkiyya, the father of Ikkesh, which is uncontested.
messages.quote: Perhaps we learned … a drilled hole and its obstruction

notes.he: לרב חסדא לא תימא שמא אלא אימא ודאי מקדח וחיסומו שנינו:
notes.en: Rav Taḥlifa said to him, to Rav Ḥisda: Do not say “perhaps”; rather say: certainly we learned “a drill and its ḥisum.”

notes.he: כלומר יכול אתה לסמוך על דבר זה:
notes.en: And you need to rely on it: that is, you can rely on this matter.

notes.he: שנסמך על עדותו שלא היה תלמיד חולק עליו:
notes.en: Like Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh: whose testimony was relied upon, since no student disputed it.

notes.dh: צריך אתה לתלות כחזקיה שהוא אבי עקש
notes.he: פירוש צריך אתה לטרוח כדי ליישב הדבר שאין לשבשה מכח קושיא כי ברור לי שכך אמר שמואל כמו עדות חזקיה אבי עקש שלא היה לשון דבריו מיושב ומתרץ ליה בסמוך:
notes.en: You need to rely on it like Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh: meaning, you need to take pains to settle the matter rather than declare it corrupt because of a difficulty, for it is clear to me that Shmuel said so. It is like the testimony of Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh, whose wording was not settled, and [the Gemara] resolves it shortly.

notes.he: יפה תירצתה וצריך אתה להיתלות עליה על תירוץ זה כמו שאנו סומכין על עדותו של חזקיה אבי עקש. כלומר שמה שאמרת הוא עיקר כאותו עדות של חזקיה:
notes.en: Rav Taḥlifa said to him: You answered well, and you need to rely on it, on this answer, as we rely on the testimony of Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh. That is, what you said is the main point, like that testimony of Ḥizkiyya.

messages.text: It can be derived from here that just as the phrase: Size of a drilled hole, is referring to the size of a hole into which the drill can be inserted and removed, so too, the size of a bitter vetch mentioned in the mishna is referring to a hole into which the bitter vetch can be inserted and removed.
§ This refers to the testimony of Ḥizkiyya the father of Ikkesh, as we learned in a baraita:

With regard to earthenware vessels, any vessel that does not have a receptacle has no distinction with regard to the halakhic status of its sides. This is in contrast to the earthenware vessels mentioned in the Torah, where only the inside, and not the outside, is susceptible to ritual impurity. Rather, if its inside, i.e., the sides that are used, became impure, its outside also becomes impure. Likewise, if its outside became impure, its inside also becomes impure.
messages.lead: Ḥizkiyya, the father of Ikkesh, testified this testimony before Rabban Gamliel in Yavne, which he said in the name of Rabban Gamliel the Elder:

notes.he: שאין אחוריו חלוקים מתוכו דלא אמרינן אם נטמא גבו גבו טמא ותוכו טהור אלא אם נטמא גבו נטמא תוכו. אותו צד שמשתמשין בו קרי תוך אע"ג דאין לו בית קיבול:
notes.en: It has no backs for a distinction: its back is not distinguished from its inside. We do not say that if its back became impure, its back is impure and its inside pure; rather, if its back became impure, its inside became impure. The side that one uses is called the “inside,” even though it has no receptacle.

notes.dh: כל שאין לו תוך בכלי חרס
notes.he: שאין לו בית קיבול אין לו אחורים לחליקה. כלומר שאין חלוק עליונו מתחתונו:
notes.en: Any that has no inside, in an earthenware vessel: which has no receptacle, has no backs for a distinction; that is, its upper side is not distinguished from its lower side.

notes.he: כלומר כשנטמא צד אחד נטמא צד השני:
notes.en: Rather, when its inside became impure, its back became impure: that is, when one side became impure, the second side became impure.

messages.text: With regard to an earthenware vessel, the Merciful One rendered its susceptibility to impurity dependent on the presence of a receptacle, as it states: “And every earthen vessel into whose interior any of them falls.” Consequently, if there is a receptacle, it will become impure, but if there is no receptacle, it should not become impure.
messages.quote: With regard to earthenware vessels, any vessel that does not have a receptacle

verse.he: וְכׇל־כְּלִי־חֶרֶשׂ אֲשֶׁר־יִפֹּל מֵהֶם אֶל־תּוֹכוֹ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכוֹ יִטְמָא וְאֹתוֹ תִשְׁבֹּרוּ׃
verse.en: And if any of those falls into an earthen vessel, everything inside it shall be impure and [the vessel] itself you shall break.

notes.dh: וקפריך כלי חרס בתוכו תלה רחמנא
notes.he: דאין מטמא אלא מתוכו דכתיב וכל כלי חרס אשר יפול מהם אל תוכו וגו':
notes.en: And he objects: With an earthenware vessel, the Merciful One made it depend on its inside: for it becomes impure only from its inside, as it is written: “And every earthen vessel into whose inside any of them falls…”

notes.he: כלי חרס כי אין לו תוך אמאי מטמא כלל בתוכו תלה רחמנא טומאה כדכתיב וכלי חרס אשר יפול מהם אל תוכו וגו' לית ליה תוך לא איטמי כלל:
notes.en: An earthenware vessel, when it has no inside, why does it become impure at all? The Merciful One made its impurity depend on its inside, as it is written: “And an earthen vessel into whose inside any of them falls…” If it has no inside, it does not become impure at all.

messages.text: The testimony is not referring to earthenware vessels, but to vessels that are purified through immersion in a ritual bath, such as wooden vessels, which are susceptible to ritual impurity even if they lack a receptacle. Accordingly, this is what the tanna is saying: With regard to earthenware vessels, any vessel that does not have a receptacle never becomes impure.

notes.he: בשאין לו תוך אין לו אחוריים לחליקה:
notes.en: Its counterpart in a vessel of rinsing: one that has no inside has no backs for a distinction.

messages.text: The halakha in the corresponding case with regard to a vessel that is purified though rinsing, i.e., immersion in a ritual bath, where it lacks a receptacle, is that there is no distinction with regard to the halakhic status of its sides. Therefore, if its inside, i.e., the side that is used, became impure, its outside also becomes impure. Likewise, if its outside became impure, its inside also becomes impure.

notes.he: כלומר דכוותיה בכלי שטף שאין לו נמי תוך אין לו אחוריים ולקמן מפרש לה. כלי שטף כלי עץ דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:י״ב) וכל כלי עץ ישטף במים ולקמיה פריך וכי אין לו תוך מי מקבל פשוטי כלי עץ טומאה. ואיכא דאמרי כלי שטף היינו כלי מתכות וטעות הוא בידם דא"כ אמאי פריך לקמן מי מקבלי פשוטי כלי שטף טומאה לאו פירכא היא דודאי פשוטי כלי מתכות טמאים:
notes.en: Its counterpart in a vessel of rinsing: that is, likewise, a vessel of rinsing that also has no inside has no [distinct] backs; and below this is explained. A vessel of rinsing is a wooden vessel, as it is written (Leviticus 15:12): “And every wooden vessel shall be rinsed in water.” And below it objects: but if it has no inside, do flat wooden vessels receive impurity? Some say a vessel of rinsing is a metal vessel, but they are mistaken: if so, why does it object below, “Do flat vessels of rinsing receive impurity?” That would be no objection, since flat metal vessels are certainly susceptible to impurity.

notes.he: בכלי עץ נופל לשון זה דכתיב בהו [וכל] כלי עץ ישטף במים כדפירש בקונטרס ומצינו למימר נמי דכלי מתכות כמו כן מיקרו כלי שטף משום דכתיב בהו ומורק ושוטף במים והא דפריך לקמן ואין לו תוך בכלי שטף מדאורייתא בר קבולי טומאה היא דומיא דשק בעינן פשיטא ליה דאיירי נמי בכלי עץ בכל הנהו דמיקרו כלי שטף מדלא נקט כלי מתכות:
notes.en: Its counterpart in a vessel of rinsing, etc.: this term fits wooden vessels, of which it is written, “And every wooden vessel shall be rinsed in water,” as the Kuntres [Rashi] explained. But we could also say that metal vessels are likewise called vessels of rinsing, since of them it is written, “it shall be scoured and rinsed in water.” And as for what it objects below, “And is a vessel of rinsing with no inside susceptible to impurity by Torah law? We require it to be like a sack”: it is obvious to [the Gemara] that it speaks also of wooden vessels among all those called vessels of rinsing, since it did not say “metal vessels.”

notes.he: תוך קרי אותו צד שרגילין להשתמש בו:
notes.en: It has no backs for a distinction; [if its inside] became impure: the side one usually uses is called its “inside.”

notes.he: כלי שטף היינו כלי מתכות או של עץ שיש לו טהרה כדכתיב ומורק ושוטף במים:
notes.en: A vessel of rinsing is a metal or wooden vessel that can be purified, as it is written: “it shall be scoured and rinsed in water.”

messages.text: Why do I need to render this halakha dependent on an earthenware vessel? Let us simply say: With regard to a vessel that is purified though rinsing, any vessel that does not have a receptacle has no distinction with regard to the halakhic status of its sides.
messages.quote: With regard to earthenware vessels, any vessel that does not have a receptacle

messages.text: This association teaches us that if the vessel that is purified through rinsing has a receptacle, it is like an earthenware vessel. Therefore, just as in the case of an earthenware vessel, if its inside became impure, its outside also becomes impure, but if its inside did not become impure, its outside does not become impure, so too, with regard to a vessel that is purified through rinsing, if its inside became impure, its outside becomes impure. But if its inside did not become impure, its outside does not become impure.

notes.he: להכי תלייה לכלי שטף בכלי חרס דהיכא דיש לו תוך נטמא תוכו נטמא גבו:
notes.en: This teaches us, etc.: this is why he made the vessel of rinsing depend on the earthenware vessel: where it has an inside, if its inside became impure, its back became impure.

notes.dh: הרי הוא ככלי חרס נטמא תוכו נטמא גבו
notes.he: על כרחו לטמא אחרים קאמר דלא נפקא מינה מידי למילתא אחריתי וקשה מכאן לגירסת רבינו שמואל דשבת (דף טז.) דמשמע דכלי חרס אין מטמאין מגבייהו כלל ובספ"ק דחולין (דף כד.) דאמרי' דאויר כלי חרס טמא [וגבו טהור] היינו דלא מקבל טומאה מגבו אבל מטמא אחרים מגבו כדתניא בתורת כהנים מרובה מדת לטמא ממדת ליטמא שמטמא אחרים מאחוריו ואינו מיטמא מאחוריו ועוד אמרי' בפרק המפלת (נדה דף כו.) דאבן היוצא מן התנור טפח דחשיב יד להוציא טומאה דלא עדיפא מגב ואין לומר דעדיפא ואיירי אפי' להכניס דהתניא בתוספתא דאין טומאה לכלי חרס אלא מאוירו ובהיסטו ועוד דדרשינן הא יש צמיד פתיל עליו טהור ומי לא עסקינן דיחדינהו לאשתו נדה ואע"ג דבריש סוגיא דהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קיח.) משמע דסבר הש"ס דיד כל תנור להכניס ולהוציא ועדיף מגבו במסקנא צרכינן למימר הכי:
notes.en: It is like an earthenware vessel: if its inside became impure, its back became impure. This must mean [its back is impure] to render other things impure, since it makes no difference for anything else. And this is difficult for the reading of Rabbeinu Shmuel in Shabbat (16a), which implies that earthenware vessels do not render impure from their backs at all. And at the end of the first chapter of Ḥullin (24a), where we say that the airspace of an earthenware vessel is impure [and its back is pure], that means it does not receive impurity from its back, but it does render others impure from its back, as is taught in Torat Kohanim: the measure for rendering impure is greater than the measure for becoming impure, for it renders others impure from its back but does not become impure from its back. Further, we say in chapter HaMappelet (Niddah 26a) that a stone protruding a handbreadth from an oven counts as a handle for conveying impurity out, and it is no better than the back. One cannot say it is better and speaks even of conveying in, for it is taught in the Tosefta that an earthenware vessel has impurity only from its airspace and by being moved. Further, we expound: “but if it has a sealed cover, it is pure,” and are we not dealing [also] with a case where he designated them for his menstruating wife? And although at the beginning of the passage of HaOr VehaRotev (Ḥullin 118a) the Talmud seems to hold that the handle of any oven serves for conveying in and out and is better than its back, in the conclusion we must say as above.

notes.he: והיכי מצית אמרת דהא קמ"ל דיש לו תוך הרי הוא ככלי חרס וכו':
notes.en: And how could you say so? This teaches us that one that has an inside is like an earthenware vessel, etc.

messages.text: Granted that with regard to an earthenware vessel, the Merciful One revealed that it is rendered ritually impure only if the impure item fell into its “inside” (see Leviticus 11:33). But with regard to a vessel that is purified though rinsing, did the Merciful One reveal with regard to it that it becomes impure only through its inside? Therefore, even if the impure item touched the outside, it should become entirely impure.

notes.he: בשלמא כלי חרס גלי ביה תוכו דבתוכו תלה רחמנא דאי איטמי תוכו נטמא כולו ואי לא נטמא תוכו אלא גבו לא נטמא תוכו אלא כלי שטף דלא גלי ביה תוכו לית ליה חלוקה:
notes.en: Granted, with an earthenware vessel, the Merciful One revealed “its inside,” for the Merciful One made it depend on its inside: if its inside became impure, all of it is impure; and if not its inside but its back became impure, its inside is not impure. But a vessel of rinsing, of which “its inside” was not revealed, has no distinction.

messages.text: If it is referring to ritual impurity that is by Torah law, then indeed a vessel that is purified through rinsing can become impure even through its outside. But here we are dealing with the ritual impurity of liquids, i.e., liquids that became impure and subsequently touched the vessel, which becomes impure only by rabbinic law. As we learned in a mishna:

notes.he: דפשיטא לן שאם נטמא גבו נטמא תוכו בין יש לו תוך בין אין לו תוך והכא במאי עסקינן דביש לו תוך נטמא גבו לא נטמא תוכו ובאין לו תוך איצטריך לאשמועי' דנטמא תוכו נטמא גבו נטמא גבו נטמא תוכו בטומאה דרבנן כלי שנטמאו אחוריו במשקין טמאין:
notes.en: If it is about Torah-law impurity, indeed: for it is obvious to us that if its back became impure its inside became impure, whether it has an inside or has no inside. And here, what are we dealing with? [A case where,] with an inside, if its back became impure its inside did not become impure; and with no inside, it was necessary to teach us that if its inside became impure its back became impure, and if its back became impure its inside became impure. This is with rabbinic impurity: a vessel whose backs became impure through impure liquids.

notes.he: כגון זב ומת הכי נמי דלית ליה חלוקה:
notes.en: If it is about Torah-law impurity, such as a zav or a corpse: indeed, it has no distinction.

messages.text: With regard to a vessel whose outside became ritually impure by contact with impure liquids, only its outside is impure, but its inside, its rim, its ear-shaped handle, and its straight handle are pure. If its inside became impure, it becomes impure in its entirety.

notes.he: דהיינו בית קיבול התחתון שיושב עליו. ל"א אוגנו שפתו:
notes.en: Its inside, its ogen: that is, the lower receptacle on which it sits. Another version: its ogen is its rim.

notes.he: זהו מה שעושין בחביות של חרס לבית אחיזה שקורין מנשי"ו:
notes.en: Its ear: what they make on earthenware jugs as a place to grasp, which is called (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: כגון כלי חרס שעושין לו זנב לאחוריו:
notes.en: Its handles: such as an earthenware vessel made with a tail at its back.

notes.dh: הכא במאי עסקינן בטומאת משקין דרבנן וכדתנן כלי שטף שניטמו אחוריו
notes.he: שוליו:
notes.en: Here, what are we dealing with? Rabbinic impurity of liquids, as we learned: a vessel of rinsing whose backs became impure, [that is,] its bottom.

messages.text: The reason is: By Torah law, food does not transmit impurity to a vessel, and a liquid does not transmit impurity to a vessel. And it was the Sages who decreed that an impure liquid transmits impurity to a vessel, because of the concern that people will be lenient with regard to the liquid of a zav and a zava, such as their urine or saliva, which are a primary source of impurity and impart impurity to vessels.

notes.dh: דמדאורייתא אין אוכלין ומשקין מטמאין כלי
notes.he: בפ"ק דפסחים (דף יח.):
notes.en: For by Torah law food and liquids do not render a vessel impure: in the first chapter of Pesaḥim (18a).

notes.he: כגון רוקו וזובו דהוי אב הטומאה ומטמא כלי מדאורייתא אפי' אדם דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:ח׳) וכי ירוק הזב וגו':
notes.en: Because of the liquid of a zav and a zava: such as his spittle and his discharge, which are a primary source of impurity and render a vessel impure by Torah law, and even a person, as it is written (Leviticus 15:8): “And if the zav spits…”

messages.text: Therefore, the Sages deemed the impurity of a vessel that is purified though rinsing whose outside became impure through liquid to be like the impurity of an earthenware vessel, and if its exterior became impure, its interior remains pure. But the Sages did not deem its impurity like the impurity of itself, i.e., a vessel that is purified through rinsing, by Torah law, that if its exterior became impure, the vessel becomes impure in its entirety.

notes.he: לכלי שטף הנטמא במשקין:
notes.en: Therefore the Rabbis made it: a vessel of rinsing that became impure through liquids.

notes.he: דאורייתא דאם נטמא גבו לא נטמא תוכו:
notes.en: Like an earthenware vessel: by Torah law, where if its back became impure its inside did not become impure.

notes.dh: ולא שויוה רבנן כטומאה דאורייתא דנפשיה
notes.he: דכלי שטף משום דעבדו רבנן היכירא להקל בטומאת משקין כי היכי דלא נשרוף עליה תרומה וקדשים אלא חולין. ואי קשיא אמאי לא גזור בכלי חרס טומאת משקין לאחוריו תריץ משום דהתם ליכא למיגזר משום משקה דהא אפי' נגעו משקה זב וזבה מאחוריו לא מקבלי טומאה אלא מתוכו ואי משום דכתיב וכלי חרס אשר יגע בו הזב וגו' ההוא מפורש (במסכת נדה) (דף מב) דבהסיט מישתעי דאיזהו מגעו שהוא ככולו הוי אומר זה היסט:
notes.en: And the Rabbis did not make it like its own Torah-law impurity, that of a vessel of rinsing: because the Rabbis made an indicator, to be lenient with the impurity of liquids, so that teruma and consecrated food would not be burned on its account, only non-sacred food. And if you ask: why did they not decree impurity of liquids on the back of an earthenware vessel? Answer: because there, there is nothing to decree on account of [the zav’s] liquid, since even if the liquid of a zav or a zava touched it from its back, it does not receive impurity; only from its inside. And if [you object] because it is written, “And an earthen vessel that the zav touches” (Leviticus 15:12), that is explained (in tractate Niddah, 42) to speak of moving it: what is “his touch” that is like all of him? You must say: this is moving it [hesset].

notes.he: דמשקין הבאין מחמת שרץ דמטמי גזירה משום משקה זב דהוי מדאורייתא הלכך כיון דאיטמו במשקין דרבנן האי כלי שטף שוויוה רבנן כטומאה דכלי חרס דיש לו חלוקה ולא שוויוה כטומאה דאורייתא כלומר דאין לו חלוקה לכלי שטף מן התורה בין יש לו תוך בין אין לו תוך ולהכי שוויוה רבנן ככלי חרס דנטמא גבו לא ניטמא תוכו משום היכירא כי היכי דלא לשרוף עליה תרומה וקדשים:
notes.en: And it is the Rabbis who decreed: that liquids that come from a creeping animal render impure, a decree because of the liquid of a zav, which is [impure] by Torah law. Therefore, since it became impure through liquids of rabbinic law, the Rabbis made this vessel of rinsing like the impurity of an earthenware vessel, which has a distinction, and did not make it like Torah-law impurity, under which a vessel of rinsing has no distinction, whether it has an inside or not. And therefore the Rabbis made it like an earthenware vessel, so that if its back became impure its inside did not become impure, as an indicator, so that teruma and consecrated food would not be burned on its account.

messages.text: The reason for this is that through this ruling the Sages employed an indicator that it is impure only by rabbinic law so that people will not burn teruma and consecrated items due to having come into contact with those vessels, as by Torah law they are ritually pure and it is prohibited to burn them.

If so, that this is the case under discussion, then with regard to a vessel that is purified through rinsing that has no receptacle as well, the Sages should employ an indicator. They should rule that the inside remains pure so that teruma and consecrated items will not be burned after coming in contact with it. Why then did Ḥizkiyya, the father of Ikkesh, testify that if its outside became impure, its inside becomes impure as well?

notes.he: לכלי שטף ליעביד ביה היכירא שום חלוק כי היכי דלא לישרוף עליה תרומה וקדשים. לא צריך דכיון דעבדו היכירא חלוקה ביש לו תוך בטומאה דרבנן מידע ידעי דכי אין לו תוך ונטמא במשקין דרבנן דאין שורפין עליו תרומה וקדשים דהשתא כי יש לו תוך אין שורפין כ"ש בשאין לו תוך:
notes.en: If so, one with no inside: for a vessel of rinsing, let them make for it some indicator of distinction, so that teruma and consecrated food would not be burned on its account. It is not necessary: since they made an indicator of distinction for one with an inside under rabbinic impurity, people know that when it has no inside and became impure through rabbinic liquids, one does not burn teruma and consecrated food on its account. For now that one does not burn when it has an inside, all the more so when it has no inside.

messages.text: Since the Sages employed an indicator with regard to vessels that are purified through rinsing that have a receptacle, it is thereby known that the impurity of a vessel that does not have a receptacle that comes in contact with an impure liquid is by rabbinic law. Therefore, no one will burn teruma and consecrated items that came in contact with it.

And with regard to a vessel that is purified through rinsing, is it susceptible to ritual impurity by Torah law, so that the Sages found it necessary to decree that the exterior is susceptible to impurity of liquids? After all, in order for a vessel to be susceptible to impurity it is required to be similar to a sack, which is mentioned with regard to ritual impurity: Just as a sack is carried both full and empty, so too, any object must be capable of being carried both full and empty in order to become ritually impure. This excludes a vessel that has no receptacle and cannot be carried full.

verse.he: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יִפֹּל־עָלָיו מֵהֶם ׀ בְּמֹתָם יִטְמָא מִכׇּל־כְּלִי־עֵץ אוֹ בֶגֶד אוֹ־עוֹר אוֹ שָׂק כׇּל־כְּלִי אֲשֶׁר־יֵעָשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בָּהֶם בַּמַּיִם יוּבָא וְטָמֵא עַד־הָעֶרֶב וְטָהֵר׃
verse.en: And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall be impure: be it any article of wood, or a cloth, or a skin, or a sack—any such article that can be put to use shall be dipped in water, and it shall remain impure until evening; then it shall be pure.

notes.dh: ואין לו תוך בכלי שטף דאורייתא בר קבולי טומאה הוא
notes.he: דאיצטריך רבנן למיגזר בהו משקין ועוד דאמרן לעיל אי בטומאה דאורייתא ה"נ לא איצטריך לאשמועינן דאין לו אחורים לחליקה:
notes.en: And is a vessel of rinsing that has no inside susceptible to impurity by Torah law, that the Rabbis needed to decree [the impurity of] liquids on them? And further, we said above: if it is about Torah-law impurity, indeed; so there would be no need to teach us that it has no backs for a distinction.

notes.he: דכתיב (ויקרא י״א:ל״ב) מכל כלי עץ או בגד או עור או שק איתקש כלי עץ לשק:
notes.en: We require it to be like a sack: as it is written (Leviticus 11:32): “of any wooden vessel, or garment, or hide, or sack”; the wooden vessel is juxtaposed to a sack.

notes.he: דיש לו בית קיבול:
notes.en: Full and empty: that it has a receptacle.

notes.he: ואי אין לו תוך בכלי שטף מדאורייתא בר קיבולי טומאה הוא בתמיהא כדקאמר בטומאה דאורייתא הכי נמי:
notes.en: And is a vessel of rinsing with no inside susceptible to impurity by Torah law? This is said in astonishment, as he said: with Torah-law impurity, indeed.

messages.text: It is referring to these vessels that are suited for sitting and are susceptible to ritual impurity imparted by treading, i.e., the ritual impurity imparted by a zav, zava, or a menstruating woman who sits or lies down on an item, even though it lacks a receptacle.

notes.he: כגון כסא וספסל דמקבלי טומאה ע"י מדרס:
notes.en: With those fit for treading: such as a chair and a bench, which receive impurity through treading.

notes.he: אבל שאר פשוטי כלי עץ טהורי' ודינם פירשתי בפ' המוכר את הבית (ב"ב סו.) ובפ' בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לא.):
notes.en: With those fit for treading: but other flat wooden vessels are pure; I explained their law in chapter HaMokher et HaBayit (Bava Batra 66a) and in chapter BeKhol Me’arvin (Eruvin 31a).

notes.he: והא כיון דאין לו תוך אינו מטלטל מלא וריקן. בהנך כלי שטף דחזו למדרסות לישיבה מקבל טומאה דאורייתא דאע"ג דלית בהו תוך כדאמרינן במסכת שבת בפ' אמר ר' עקיבא כגון דיחדינהו לאשתו נדה:
notes.en: But we require it to be like a sack, and since it has no inside it is not carried full and empty. [The answer:] with those vessels of rinsing that are fit for treading, for sitting, which receive Torah-law impurity even though they have no inside, as we say in tractate Shabbat, in chapter Amar Rabbi Akiva: for example, where he designated them for his menstruating wife.

messages.text: If so, with regard to an earthenware vessel that has no inside, the Rabbis should also decree that it is susceptible to the impurity of liquids if it is fit for sitting. There is no ritual impurity imparted by treading with regard to earthenware vessels.

notes.he: נגזור טומאה באין לו תוך בהנך דחזו למדרסות:
notes.en: If so, with an earthenware vessel too: let us decree impurity on one with no inside, among those fit for treading.

notes.he: שישבר אם אדם יושב עליו:
notes.en: There is no treading in an earthenware vessel: for it would break if a person sat on it.

notes.he: כי אין לו תוך אמאי אינו מטמא לדעתיה דר' יצחק בר אבין וקאמר משום דאין מדרס בכלי חרש מפרש נמי התם:
notes.en: If so, an earthenware vessel too: when it has no inside, why does it not become impure, according to Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avin? And he says: because there is no treading in an earthenware vessel, as is also explained there.

messages.text: § Returning to the matter of an incomplete skull: according to the opinion of Beit Shammai, if the skull is missing a piece of bone the size of a drilled hole, it does not impart impurity. According to Shmuel, Beit Hillel holds that it must be missing a piece the size of a sela coin. If so, there would be no disagreement between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, as it was taught with regard to a window that imparts ritual impurity that a drilled hole is the same size as a sela coin. An additional answer:
It was with regard to a large drill that we learned that the minimum size of a window that imparts impurity equals the size of a sela coin.

notes.he: הא דאמרת עשית ב"ש וב"ה אחד לאו פירכא היא:
notes.en: Rav Pappa says: what you said, “You have made Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel one,” is not a refutation.

notes.he: במשנה דמאור העשוי בידי אדם דמקדח גדול דהוי כסלע נירונית אבל מקדח סתם בציר מסלע וב"ש במקדח סתם קאמרי:
notes.en: That we learned of a large drill: in the mishna of the window made by people, it is a large drill that is like a Neronian sela. But an unspecified drill is less than a sela, and Beit Shammai speak of an unspecified drill.

notes.he: לא צריך לתרוצי להא מקדח וחיסומו שנינו אלא מקדח גדול שנינו כאן דהוי בסלע מכלל דמקדח סתם ההוא דב"ש בן גדול מכלל דזוטר מבסלע וב"ה אמר כסלע ואין שיעורן אחד:
notes.en: Rav Pappa says: there is no need to answer that “we learned a drill and its ḥisum.” Rather, we learned here of a large drill, which is a sela. By inference, the unspecified drill, Beit Shammai’s, is not a large one, so it is smaller than a sela; and Beit Hillel say a sela, and their measures are not one.

messages.text: By inference, the unspecified drill mentioned in the statement of Beit Shammai with regard to an incomplete skull is also smaller than the size of a sela coin mentioned by Beit Hillel.

notes.he: דמוקים לה לההוא מקדח דגלגלת כמקדח קטן של רופאים דהוי בציר מבסלע וב"ה אמרי בסלע היינו דאיכא בינייהו:
notes.en: This works out for Rabbi Meir: who establishes that drill of the skull as the small drill of doctors, which is less than a sela, while Beit Hillel say a sela; that is the difference between them.

messages.text: This works out well according to the explanation of Rabbi Meir for the opinion of Beit Shammai. But according to the opinion of the Rabbis, what is there to say?

notes.he: דאמרינן בגדול של לשכה דהיינו כסלע מאי איכא למימר:
notes.en: But according to the Rabbis: who say the large one of the chamber, which is a sela, what is there to say?

messages.text: As we learned in a mishna:
With regard to which drill did Beit Shammai state their opinion concerning an incomplete skull?
It was with regard to a small drill of doctors, used for drilling bones. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: ב"ש בגולגולת כמלא מקדח כקטן של רופאים שקודרין בו את הראש לתקן את המכה:
notes.en: With which drill did they say: Beit Shammai, regarding the skull, “the size of a drill”: like the small one of doctors, with which they bore into the head to treat a wound.

messages.text: It was with regard to a large drill, such as that used in the Temple chamber.
According to the mishna concerning a window that imparts impurity, the size of this drill is like that of a sela coin, and the opinions of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel would still be identical.

And even according to the opinion of Rabbi Meir, does it work out well? If the unspecified drill mentioned by Beit Shammai is smaller than a sela coin, then this is an instance of the leniencies of Beit Shammai and of the stringencies of Beit Hillel, as with regard to a skull that was missing a piece only the size of a drilled hole, Beit Shammai are lenient and hold that it does not impart impurity in a tent, while Beit Hillel do consider it impure.

notes.dh: הניחא לר"מ כו' ותו אפי' לר"מ מי ניחא
notes.he: אם כן דשיעורא דב"ש זוטר הוה ליה מקולי ב"ש דהיינו קולא דבשיעורא זוטא כי האי פרחה לה טומאת גולגולת:
notes.en: This works out for Rabbi Meir, etc., and further, even for Rabbi Meir, does it work out? If so, that Beit Shammai’s measure is smaller, it would be one of the leniencies of Beit Shammai. That is a leniency, since with so small a measure the skull’s impurity departs.

messages.text: And we have a principle: That which we learned in the mishna in tractate Eduyyot pertaining to the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel, we learned, and that which we did not learn there, we did not learn. Therefore, in all other cases, Beit Shammai are stringent and Beit Hillel are lenient.

notes.he: בעדיות (פ"ה משנה א) ששה דברים מקולי ב"ש שב לא תנן:
notes.en: And we learned six: in Eduyyot (5:1), six matters among the leniencies of Beit Shammai; seven we did not learn. [Rashi reads “and we learned six,” where the Davidson English reads “that which we learned, we learned.”]

notes.he: דמוקים במקדח קטן א"כ הוה ליה מקולי ב"ש ומחומרי ב"ה. דב"ש מקילינן דכי חסר פורתא במקדח קטן טהור מלטמא באהל וב"ה מחמירי דלעולם לא טהר מלטמא עד שתחסר כסלע ואנן דתנן תנן כלומר אותן ששה דברים שהן מקולי ב"ש מנו ולא יותר:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Meir: who establishes it as a small drill, it would be one of the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel. For Beit Shammai are lenient: when a little is missing, the size of a small drill, it is pure and does not impart impurity in a tent; and Beit Hillel are stringent: it never becomes pure from imparting impurity until a sela’s worth is missing. And “what we learned, we learned”: that is, they counted those six matters that are leniencies of Beit Shammai, and no more.

messages.text: It is specifically with regard to a sela of the emperor Nero that we learned in the mishna concerning a window that imparts impurity that it is like the size of a large drilled hole. But with regard to the unspecified sela coin mentioned by Beit Hillel as the measure, it is even smaller than an unspecified drilled hole. Therefore, Beit Shammai are stringent even according to the opinion of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: דהוי כמקדח גדול אבל כסלע דקאמרי ב"ה זוטר אפי' ממקדח קטן של רופאים הלכך אפי' לר"מ שיעורא דב"ש נפיש:
notes.en: We learned of a Neronian sela: which is like a large drill. But the sela that Beit Hillel speak of is smaller, even than the small drill of doctors. Therefore, even according to Rabbi Meir, Beit Shammai’s measure is larger.

notes.he: אלא רב נחמן מתרץ לטעמיה דר' מאיר דסלע נרונית שנינו הכא במאור שנעשה דהויא במקדח גדול סלע סתם דב"ה הוי זוטר אפי' ממקדח סתם דב"ש והוו להו ב"ה לקולא:
notes.en: Rather, Rav Naḥman answers according to Rabbi Meir’s view: we learned of a Neronian sela here, regarding a window that was made, which is like a large drill. The unspecified sela of Beit Hillel is smaller even than Beit Shammai’s unspecified drill, so Beit Hillel are on the lenient side.

messages.text: Mishna
For these blemishes of the eye, one may slaughter the firstborn animal outside the Temple: The eyelid that was pierced, an eyelid that was damaged and is lacking, or an eyelid that was split;

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Mishna. The ris of the eye: it is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: זהו עפעפיו:
notes.en: The ris of the eye: this is its eyelids.

messages.text: and likewise, one may slaughter a firstborn animal outside the Temple if there was in his eye a cataract, a tevallul,

notes.he: כלומר הרי שיש בעינו דק טייל"א:
notes.en: Behold, in his eye is a dak: that is, behold, there is a dak in his eye (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: מפרש מאי היא:
notes.en: Tevallul: it explains what it is.

notes.he: כמו או שהיה בעינו דק. בלע"ז טיילא:
notes.en: Behold, in his eye: as if to say, or there was a dak in his eye (Rabbeinu Gershom adds an Old French gloss).

messages.text: or a growth in the shape of a snail, a snake, or a berry that covers the pupil.

notes.he: חולי היא שקורין לימו"ן:
notes.en: Ḥilazon [snail]: it is an illness, which is called (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Naḥash [snake]: it is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: מיי"ל:
notes.en: And inav [berry]: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Ḥilazon, naḥash, inav: it is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: חלזון קורין בלעז לימץ:
notes.en: Ḥilazon is called in the vernacular (Rabbeinu Gershom adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: שיש בעינו כענבה שמנומר עינו כנחש:
notes.en: Inav [berry]: that there is in his eye something like a berry, that his eye is spotted like a snake.

messages.text: What is a tevallul? It is a white thread that bisects the iris and enters the black pupil. If it is a black thread that bisects the iris and enters the white of the eye it is not a blemish.

notes.he: סירא היינו שורה שבעין סביב לשחור. שחור הוא שקורין פרוניל"א שמשם מראית העין באה. ואם חוט של לבן יוצא מן הלבן ופוסק אותה שורה ונכנס בשחור הוי מום:
notes.en: A white that cuts across the sira: the sira is the ring in the eye around the black. The black is what is called (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), from which the sight of the eye comes. And if a thread of white goes out from the white, cuts across that ring and enters the black, it is a blemish.

notes.he: אם חוט השחור יוצא מן השחור ופוסק בסירא ונכנס בלבן:
notes.en: Black that enters the white: if a thread of black goes out from the black, cuts across the sira and enters the white.

notes.he: שאין מומין בלבן דלאו עין הוא אלא שומן העין:
notes.en: It is not a blemish: for there are no blemishes in the white, since it is not the eye but the fat of the eye.

notes.he: הפוסק בסירא ונכנס בשחור מן הלבן סירה הוא כמו חוט שסובב השחור:
notes.en: That cuts across the sira and enters the black from the white: the sira is like a thread that surrounds the black.

notes.he: אבל אם השחור פוסק הסירה ונכנס בלבן אינו מום שאין מומין בלבן שהלבן אין קרוי עין אלא השחור:
notes.en: But if the black cuts across the sira and enters the white, it is not a blemish, for there are no blemishes in the white, since the white is not called “eye,” only the black.

messages.text: Gemara
What is the meaning of: The ris?
messages.quote: The eyelid that was pierced, an eyelid that was damaged … or an eyelid that was split

messages.text: It means the outer line, or barrier, of the eye, i.e., the eyelid.

notes.he: שורה חיצונה של עין היינו בת עין המכסה את העין:
notes.en: Tora bara de’eina: the outer line of the eye, that is, the eyelid that covers the eye.

notes.he: שורה שחוץ מן העין שמכסה העין וזהו בת עין:
notes.en: Tora bara de’eina: the line outside the eye that covers the eye; this is the eyelid.

messages.text: The mishna stated: A cataract, a tevallul. With regard to a cataract, the Sages taught:
A sunken cataract, i.e., one that is in the eye itself, is a blemish, but a floating cataract, i.e., one that is floating above the eye, is not a blemish.

notes.he: דק המשקע את העין הרי זה מום:
notes.en: A sunken dak: a dak that sinks into the eye is a blemish.

messages.text: But isn’t the opposite taught in a baraita, that a sunken cataract is not a blemish whereas a floating one is a blemish?
messages.quote: A sunken cataract is a blemish, but a floating cataract is not a blemish

messages.text: That is not difficult, as this first baraita is referring to a cataract in the black portion of the eye, whereas that second baraita is referring to one in the white portion of the eye.

notes.he: השתא קס"ד דמוקים חדא בשחור של עין וחדא בלבן של עין:
notes.en: This in the black, that in the white: at this point [the Gemara] thinks to establish one in the black of the eye and one in the white of the eye.

messages.text: But it was taught that there are no blemishes in the white portion of the eye. Rather, both baraitot are referring to the black portion of the eye, and this second baraita is referring to a white cataract, whereas that first baraita is referring to a black cataract.

notes.dh: אלא הא בדק שחור הא בדק לבן דאמר רבה בר בר חנה כו'
notes.he: מתרץ הא דת"ר ודתניא איפכא:
notes.en: Rather, this is a black dak and that is a white dak, as Rabba bar bar Ḥana said, etc.: this reconciles what the Sages taught with what is taught in reverse.

messages.text: This is as Rabba bar bar Ḥana says:

Yoshiya from Usha told me that with regard to a black cataract, if it is sunken it is a blemish, but if it is floating it is not a blemish. Conversely, with regard to a white cataract, if it is sunken it is not a blemish, whereas if it is floating it is a blemish.
And your mnemonic to remember this is barka, which is a disease in which white patches float above the eye, and it is considered a blemish.

notes.he: מייל"א דהוי לבן וצף והוי מום הכא נמי סימן זה יהא לך בדוק דלבן וצף הוי מום:
notes.en: And your mnemonic is barka: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), which is white and floating and is a blemish. So here too, let this be your sign: of a dak, a white floating one is a blemish.

notes.he: כגון השוכר את החמור והבריקה (ב"מ דף עח.):
notes.en: Barka: as in “one who hires a donkey and it developed barka” (Bava Metzia 78a).

notes.he: משמע דהוי מום קבוע ותימה דבפ' מי שאחזו (גיטין סט.) יש רפואות לברקא ובפרק המוציא יין (שבת עח.) נמי אמרי' כוחלין לברקותי וי"ל דהתם מיירי בממשמשין ובאין קודם שנקבעו וכן נמי [צריך] לתרץ אקושיא אחריתי דהתם בפרק המוציא יין קתני (ג"ז שם) דם כדי לכחול עין אחת שכך כוחלין (ליחוור) [ליארוד] ובתוספתא (דשבת פ"ט) גרסי' להו ובתוספתא במכילתין (פ"ד) כתוב יאור במקום חורוור משמע דהכל אחד וחורוור הקבוע חשיב לקמן מום ומיהו איכא למימר דבשבת מיירי באותו שאינו קבוע ועוד יש לתרץ דהיכא דאין מתרפא מאליו חשיב מום והא דקאמר לקמן גבי מים הקבועים דאם עובר כשמאכילין אותו לח ויבש של גשמים לא הוי קבוע אין זו רפואה ממש אלא בדיקה ונסיון אם הם קבועים אם לאו אבל רפואה גמורה יכולה להעביר מום קבוע תדע דלקמן (בכורות דף לט:) אמרינן גבי נפגם הזובן נפגם ולא ניטל דניטל חוזר לאיתנו יותר וכשנפגם נמי הוי יכול ליטלו ומיהו י"ל דכי נפגם תחלה אין לו תקנה וקצת יש לדקדק מילפת דכתיבא באורייתא והוי מום כדלקמן (בכורות דף מא.) והיא חזזית המצרית ובב"ק בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא דף פ:) משמע דיש לה רפואה כדאמרינן מתריעין על החיכוך בשבת ומוקי לה בחזזית המצרית דלח מבחוץ ויבש מבפנים ומיהו יש לפרש דהא שמתריעין לאו שתתרפא אלא שלא תוסיף דמה נפשך אין לה רפואה דאמרי' לקמן שמלפפת והולכת עד יום המיתה וכתיב נמי אשר לא תוכל להרפא ומיהו יש לדקדק מיבלת דכתיבא והויא מום כדלקמן ותנן בפ' המוצא תפילין (עירובין קג.) חותכין יבלת במקדש וכן חותכין יבלת בפסח (פסחים סה:) אלמא יש לה רפואה בחתיכה וחשיב מום ואין להעמידה דלית בה עצם דתלתולי בעלמא הוא כדלקמן ומיהו יש להעמידה ביבלת שבעין ודלית ביה שער דאין שוחטין עלה לא במקדש ולא במדינה ואע"ג דאמרי' בעירובין (שם) לחה ויבשה יד וכלי הכל שייך ביבלת שבעין:
notes.en: In brief: “And your mnemonic is barka” implies that barka is a permanent blemish. Tosafot asks: in Gittin (69a) there are remedies for barka, and in Shabbat (78a) we also say that one paints the eye for barkit. Answer: there it speaks of one that is just beginning, before it has set. The same answer is needed for another difficulty: in Shabbat (78a) it teaches [one is liable for carrying] blood enough to paint one eye, for so they paint for yarod (the Tosefta of Shabbat, chapter 9, has this reading), and the Tosefta of our tractate (chapter 4) writes yaor in place of ḥavarvar, which implies they are all one; and a constant ḥavarvar is counted below as a blemish. One may answer that Shabbat speaks of one that is not constant; or, alternatively, that wherever it does not heal by itself it counts as a blemish. As for what is said below of constant tears, that if they pass when the animal is fed moist and dry fodder of rain they are not constant: that is not true healing but a test of whether they are constant, while a full remedy can remove a permanent blemish. Proof: below (39b), of the gums, damaged but not removed, removal restores [the animal] to firmer health, and when merely damaged it could also be removed; though one may answer that once damaged first, it has no remedy. One might also infer from yalefet, written in the Torah and a blemish (41a), which is the Egyptian ḥazazit: Bava Kamma (80b) implies it has a remedy, since an alarm is sounded for itching on Shabbat, and that is established as the Egyptian ḥazazit, moist outside and dry inside. But one may explain that the alarm is not so that it will heal but so that it will not spread, for either way it has no remedy: we say below that it clings until the day of death, and it is written, “from which you cannot be healed.” Yet one may infer from a wart, which is written [in the Torah] and is a blemish, as below, and Eruvin (103a) teaches that one cuts off a wart in the Temple, and likewise on Passover (Pesaḥim 65b): evidently it is remedied by cutting, and it still counts as a blemish. It cannot be established as one with no bone, which is mere hanging flesh, as below; but it can be established as a wart in the eye that has no hair, for which one slaughters neither in the Temple nor in the country, even though Eruvin speaks of moist or dry, by hand or with a tool, all of which applies to a wart in the eye. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: כלומר באותו דק לבן שקורין ברקא הוי מום והיינו דק לבן:
notes.en: And your mnemonic is barka: that is, that white dak called barka is a blemish, and that is a white dak [that floats], that is, protrudes. [A note in the printed edition supplies “that floats.”] Barka is as in “for barkit” (Shabbat 78a).

notes.he: צף. ברק כמו לברוקתי:
notes.en: Protruding: floating. Barak is as in “for barkit.”

messages.text: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: Is the snail mentioned in the mishna the same as the snake, or perhaps they are two distinct blemishes, and the mishna means a snail or a snake?
messages.quote: a snail, a snake, or a berry

messages.text: Come and hear, as Rabba bar bar Ḥana says:

Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Elazar told me: There was a certain elder in our neighborhood, and Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei Lakonya was his name, and in all my days I did not pass before him. But once I did pass before him, and he said to me:

notes.he: כהן היה:
notes.en: A certain elder: he was a priest.

notes.he: שגדול הדור היה:
notes.en: I did not pass before him: for he was the great one of the generation.

messages.text: Sit, my son, sit, and I will teach you one matter: This snail that you see in the eye of a firstborn is a permanent blemish, and it is permitted to slaughter the animal on its account. And this is also the snake mentioned by the Sages as a blemish.

notes.he: בכור היה לו לאותו זקן והיה לו חלזון בעינים:
notes.en: This snail: that elder had a firstborn, and it had a snail in its eyes.

notes.he: היה לו בכור. שהיה בעינו חלזון והיה מראהו ואמר חלזון זה מום קבוע הוא:
notes.en: This snail: he had a firstborn. [The line is garbled in the printed text; a note there suggests:] there was a dak in its eye that looked like a snail, and he said: This snail is a permanent blemish.

messages.text: And even though the Sages said that a person cannot see blemishes for himself, and therefore I cannot permit this firstborn to myself, even so a halakhic authority may issue a halakhic ruling to his students, and the students may then issue a halakhic ruling for him based on what he taught them. Consequently, once I have taught you this halakha, you may permit my firstborn to me due to this blemish.

notes.dh: ואע"פ שאמרו אין אדם רואה מום לעצמו
notes.he: שהבכור שלו היה אבל מורה הוא לתלמידים כו'. ובשביל כך קראהו להורות לו כדי שיתירנו לך וזה לאחר שאירע לו מעשה בבכורו הורה שמום קבוע הוא:
notes.en: And even though they said a person may not examine a blemish for himself, since the firstborn was his, he may rule for students, etc. And for that reason he called him: to teach him, so that he would permit it. And this was after the incident with his firstborn happened to him, [when] he ruled that it is a permanent blemish.

messages.text: How could Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Elazar permit the firstborn in this manner? But doesn’t Rabbi Abba say that Rav Huna says:
messages.quote: the students may then issue a halakhic ruling for him

messages.text: With regard to any Torah scholar who is engaged in issuing a ruling of halakha in a situation relevant to himself, if he already stated the ruling before the incident, i.e., before it was relevant to him, one listens to him; and if not, i.e., the ruling followed the incident, one does not listen to him.

notes.he: הלכה חדשה שלא שמענוה מאחר:
notes.en: Who issues a ruling of halakha: a new halakha that we have not heard from anyone else.

notes.he: קודם שבא מעשה ההלכה בידו:
notes.en: Before the incident: before the incident to which the halakha applies came into his hands.

notes.he: ועושין מעשה:
notes.en: One listens to him: and acts on it.

notes.he: דבשביל המעשה אומרה. והכא מאן ציית ליה במאי דאמר דמום קבוע הוא:
notes.en: One does not listen to him: since he says it on account of the incident. And here, who would heed him in what he said, that it is a permanent blemish?

notes.dh: אם קודם מעשה אמרה שומעין לו
notes.he: אומר ר"ת דלא אמרי' הכי אלא היכא דצריך לאותה הוראה כי הכא וביבמות בפ' הערל (יבמות דף עו.) גבי חגר חרב כישמעאל ובפרק נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות צח.) גבי גר נושא אשת אחיו מאמו ובריש עשרה יוחסין (קדושין ע:) גבי עובדא דרב יהודה דכל דאמר מבית חשמונאי אתינא עבדא הוא שהיה נראה לרב יהודה שאומר כן לפי שהקניטו:
notes.en: If he said it before the incident, one listens to him: Rabbeinu Tam says that we say this only where he needs that ruling [for himself], as here; and in Yevamot, chapter HaArel (76a), regarding “he girded a sword like Ishmael”; and in chapter Nos’in al HaAnusa (Yevamot 98a), regarding a convert marrying the wife of his maternal brother; and at the beginning of Asara Yuḥasin (Kiddushin 70b), regarding the incident of Rav Yehuda, [who said] that anyone who says “I come from the house of the Hasmoneans” is a slave, for it would have seemed that Rav Yehuda said so because the man had provoked him.

messages.text: He too, Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei Lakonya, was engaged in issuing this ruling of halakha at the outset, before it became relevant to him.

notes.dh: האי נמי מורה ובא מעיקרא הוה פעם אחרת קודם שאירע לו מעשה הורה שמום קבוע הוא
notes.he: (האי נמי מורה) ור' מאיר דבר המבלבל את העין לא שנא לבן בשחור ולא שנא שחור בלבן:
notes.en: He too was ruling from the outset: on another occasion, before the incident with his firstborn happened to him, he ruled that it is a permanent blemish. And Rabbi Meir: “a thing that confuses the eye,” whether white in the black or black in the white.

messages.text: Whose opinion is expressed in the mishna? It is the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: What is a tevallul? It is a white thread that bisects the iris

notes.he: דקתני אין מום בלבן רבי יוסי היא:
notes.en: The mishna: which teaches that there is no blemish in the white is Rabbi Yosei.

messages.text: If there is either a white thread that enters the black, or a black thread that enters the white, it is a blemish; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
If it is a white thread that enters the black, it is a blemish, but if it is a black thread that enters the white, it is not a blemish, as there are no blemishes in the white of the eye.

What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei? As it is written: “Their eyes stand forth from fatness”, which is interpreted to mean that the wicked embark on an evil path due to the fatness in the eyes, which is in the white portion. This indicates that the white portion is called the fat of the eye, but it is not called simply: Their eyes. Conversely, a tevallul is considered a blemish only if it is in the eye itself, as it states: “Or tevallul in his eye” (Leviticus 21:20).
messages.quote: there are no blemishes in the white

verse.he: יָצָא מֵחֵלֶב עֵינֵמוֹ עָבְרוּ מַשְׂכִּיּוֹת לֵבָב׃
verse.en:
Fat shuts out their eyes;
their fancies are extravagant.

notes.he: יצא רשע לתרבות רעה מרוב שומן שבעינו ושומן העין בלבן הוא:
notes.en: Their eyes stand forth from fatness: the wicked one went out to evil ways from the abundance of fat in his eye, and the fat of the eye is in the white.

notes.he: לפי הדרשה לבן שבעין קורין חלב כדפי' בקונטרס ששם שומן העין ורוצה לומר שיצא הרשע לתרבות רעה מרוב שומן שבעין אבל פשטיה דקרא רוצה לומר שיוצא העין ובולט לחוץ מרוב שומן שבתוכו:
notes.en: Their eyes stand forth from fatness: according to the exposition, the white of the eye is called fat, as the Kuntres [Rashi] explained, since the fat of the eye is there; and it means that the wicked one went out to evil ways from the abundance of fat in the eye. But the plain sense of the verse is that the eye comes out and bulges outward from the abundance of fat within it.

notes.he: היינו הלבן שבעין:
notes.en: Tarba de’eina [the fat of the eye]: that is the white in the eye.

messages.text: And with regard to Rabbi Meir, what is his reason? Rabbi Meir would explain as follows: What is the meaning of the expression tevallul? It is a substance that mixes [hamevalbel] within the eyes, i.e., which passes through the white and the black in any fashion.

notes.he: שפוסק הסירא ומערב השחור והלבן כל היכי דעבר הוי מבלבל:
notes.en: A thing that confuses: that cuts across the sira and mixes the black and the white; wherever it crosses, it confuses.

messages.caption: The tevallul: a thread that crosses the ring around the black of the eye. Rabbi Meir: a blemish in either direction. Rabbi Yosei, and the mishna: only white into black, since there are no blemishes in the white.

messages.text: Mishna
Pale spots on the eye and tears streaming from the eye that are constant are blemishes that enable the slaughter of the firstborn.

notes.he: חולי הוא שיש טיפין לבנות בעין:
notes.en: Mishna. Ḥavarvar: it is an illness in which there are white drops in the eye.

notes.he: אתרוייהו [קאי] אחורוור ואמים:
notes.en: The constant: this refers to both, the ḥavarvar and the tears.

notes.he: אם יש בשחור לבן ואית דאמרי קרום:
notes.en: Ḥavarvar: if there is white in the black; and some say, a membrane.

notes.he: שעיניו דולפין תדיר הרי זה מום:
notes.en: And constant tears: that his eyes drip constantly; this is a blemish.

messages.text: Which are the pale spots that are constant? They are any spots that persisted for eighty days.

notes.he: ולא נתמעט ממה שהיה:
notes.en: Any that lasted eighty days: and did not diminish from what it was.

messages.alt: the daf reads Ḥananya ben Antigonus
messages.text: One examines it three times within eighty days. Only if the spots are found during all three examinations are they considered constant.

notes.he: ואם לא בדקוהו אע"פ שמום נמצא שם ביום שמונים לא הוי מום דשמא בינתים הלך לו וחזר שכן דרכו:
notes.en: One examines it three times within eighty days: and if they did not examine it, even though the blemish is found there on the eightieth day, it is not a blemish, for perhaps in between it went away and came back, as is its way.

messages.text: And these are the constant tears, i.e., this is how it is known whether the blemish is temporary or permanent: In a case where the animal ate, for medicinal purposes, moist fodder and dry fodder from a field watered exclusively with rain, or if the animal ate moist fodder and dry fodder from an irrigated field, or even if the animal did not eat them together but ate the dry fodder and thereafter ate the moist fodder, and the condition of constant tears was not healed, it is not a blemish.

notes.he: שעיניו נוטפות מים:
notes.en: Tears: that its eyes drip water.

notes.he: כלומר במאי ידעינן אי קבועין הן אי עוברים:
notes.en: These are the constant tears: that is, how do we know whether they are constant or passing?

notes.he: אם האכילוהו לרפואה תבן ומספוא שקורין פיצ"א:
notes.en: Ate moist and dry of rain: if they fed it, as a remedy, straw and fodder, which is called (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: הגדל בניסן ויבש הגדל בתשרי כדמפרש בגמרא והאכילוהו ביחד לח ויבש של גשמים הגדל בשדה בית הבעל דסגי ליה בגשמים:
notes.en: Moist: what grows in Nisan; and dry: what grows in Tishrei, as explained in the Gemara. And they fed it moist and dry of rain together, grown in a rain-fed field [beit ha-ba’al], for which rain suffices.

notes.he: קרקע שצריכה להשקות:
notes.en: Or moist and dry of irrigation: ground that needs to be watered.

notes.he: או שלא אכל לח ויבש ביחד אלא אכל יבש ואח"כ אכל לח לרפואה אין זה דרך רפואה אע"פ שלא נתרפא בכך אינו מום עד שיאכל יבש אחר הלח דזו היא דרך רפואתו ואם לא נתרפא הוי מום:
notes.en: Or it did not eat moist and dry together, but ate dry and afterward ate moist as a remedy: this is not the way of remedy, so even though it was not healed by this, it is not a blemish until it eats dry after moist, for that is the way to remedy it; and if it was not healed, it is a blemish.

messages.text: It is not a blemish unless the animal eats the moist fodder and thereafter eats the dry fodder and is not thereby healed.

notes.he: והיאך בודקין אותו אם אכל עשב לח ויבש של גשמים ושל שדה בית הבעל ששותה מאליה. או אכל לח ויבש של שדה בית השלחין שמשקין אותה. או שאכל יבש של שדה של גשמים ואח"כ אכל הלח ועדיין לא נתרפא אפי' כן אינו מום עד שיאכל היבש של גשמים אחר הלח. שהלח של שדה גשמים. אכל קודם היבש אם בכך לא נתרפא הוי מום קבוע. וישנו ג' חדשים. כלומר בג' חדשים יאכלהו בכל חדש לח ואח"כ יבש:
notes.en: And these are constant tears: and how does one test it? If it ate moist and dry grass of rain, from a rain-fed field that drinks by itself; or ate moist and dry from an irrigated field that they water; or ate the dry of a rain field and afterward ate the moist, and still was not healed: even so it is not a blemish until it eats the dry of rain after the moist. For if it ate the moist of a rain field before the dry and was not healed by this, it is a permanent blemish. “And it lasts three months”: that is, over three months one feeds it each month moist and afterward dry.

messages.text: Gemara
Whose opinion is expressed in the mishna? It is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: any spots that persisted for eighty days

notes.he: דקתני חורוור קבוע שמונים יום רבי יהודה היא:
notes.en: Gemara. The mishna: which teaches that a constant ḥavarvar is eighty days, is Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: A blemish of constant pale spots is a condition that persisted for forty days, and constant tears is a condition that persisted for eighty days; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
A blemish of constant pale spots is a condition that persisted for eighty days.

And these are the constant tears: In a case where the animal ate moist fodder and dry fodder from an irrigated field, or ate the dry fodder and thereafter ate the moist fodder, and the animal was not healed, its status as a blemish is not certain. It is not a blemish unless the animal eats the dry fodder after eating the moist fodder and is not thereby healed. And the duration of this period of eating moist and then dry fodder extends for three months.

notes.dh: אכל לח ויבש של בית הבעל
notes.he: שאין צריך להשקותה ההוא הוי רפואה:
notes.en: Ate moist and dry of a rain-fed field: which does not need to be watered; that is a remedy. [Rashi’s text of the baraita reads “of a rain-fed field” here, where the Davidson English reads “from an irrigated field.”]

notes.he: דלא הוי רפואה ולא בדקנא ביה:
notes.en: And not moist and dry of irrigation: which is no remedy, and we do not test with it.

notes.he: של בית הבעל ואחר כך לח אינו נבדק בכך דאין זו דרך רפואה:
notes.en: Or ate dry: of a rain-fed field, and afterward moist: it is not tested this way, for this is not the way of remedy.

notes.he: דג' חדשים בדקינן ליה בהכי:
notes.en: And it lasts three months: for three months we test it this way.

notes.dh: ואיכא דאמרי ויש לו ג' חדשים
notes.he: כלומר דישנה לבדיקה זו ג' חדשים:
notes.en: And some say: “and it has three months,” that is, this test has three months.

messages.text: But how can the mishna be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda? We learned about two types of fields in the mishna: A case where the animal ate moist fodder and dry fodder from a field watered exclusively with rain and a case where the animal ate moist fodder and dry fodder from an irrigated field and was not healed. In either case, it is not a blemish.
messages.quote: moist fodder and dry fodder from a field watered exclusively with rain, or … from an irrigated field

notes.he: דבין של בית הבעל בין של שלחין ואי אכיל יבש אחר הלח מסי ובדקינן ומתניתין כרבי יהודה אוקימתא:
notes.en: But we learned both: [the mishna implies that] both of a rain-fed field and of irrigation, if it eats dry after moist, it heals, and we test with it; yet we established the mishna as Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.dh: והיכי מצי מוקים מתני' כר' יהודה והאנן תרויהו תנינהו
notes.he: אבל לח ויבש של גשמים לח ויבש של שלחין כו':
notes.en: And how can he establish the mishna according to Rabbi Yehuda? But we learned both of them: moist and dry of rain, moist and dry of irrigation, etc.

messages.text: By contrast, Rabbi Yehuda mentioned only moist fodder and dry fodder from a field that requires irrigation, from which it can be inferred that if the animal was fed moist fodder and dry fodder from a field watered exclusively with rain and it was not healed, its condition is a blemish.
The mishna is incomplete and this is what it is teaching, in accordance with the ruling of Rabbi Yehuda in the baraita:

notes.he: מתני':
notes.en: It is incomplete: the mishna.

notes.he: חסורי מחסרא מתניתא והכי קתני:
notes.en: The matnita is incomplete, and this is what it teaches. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s wording, matnita, usually means the baraita, so he seems to apply the correction to the baraita, to bring it in line with our mishna; the Davidson English and Rashi apply it to the mishna.]

messages.text: If the animal ate moist fodder and dry fodder from a field watered exclusively with rain, it is a blemish. If it ate moist fodder and dry fodder from an irrigated field, it is not a blemish. And with regard to a field watered exclusively with rain as well, if it ate the dry fodder and thereafter ate the moist fodder it is not a blemish. It is not a blemish until the animal eats the dry fodder after the moist fodder.

notes.he: אם לא נתרפא בכך:
notes.en: It is a blemish: if it was not healed by this.

notes.dh: והכי תרצה אכל לח ויבש של גשמים הרי זה מום כו'
notes.he: ואתיא כמתניתין:
notes.en: And answer it thus: ate moist and dry of rain, it is a blemish, etc. And it accords with our mishna.

messages.text: Is that so? But isn’t it taught that Rav Idi bar Avin says that Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashiyan says:
messages.quote: And the duration of this period … extends for three months

messages.text: The months of Adar and Nisan are the moist period mentioned in the mishna, as the fodder is still moist at that time of year; and the months of Elul and Tishrei are the dry period, as this is the end of summer.
In total, there are four months, not three.
One should say as follows: The months of Adar and half of Nisan are the moist period, and the months of Elul and half of Tishrei are the dry period, for a total of three months.

notes.he: אימא אדר וחצי ניסן לח אלול וחצי אדר יבש דהיינו ג' חדשים ותו לא וקמ"ל אע"ג דאין רצופין:
notes.en: Is that so, three months and no more? Say: Adar and half of Nisan, moist; Elul and half of Adar [so the text; read: Tishrei], dry, which is three months and no more. And it teaches us that [it counts] even though they are not consecutive.

messages.caption: Testing constant tears, as the Gemara completes the mishna: fodder from a rain-watered field, moist and then dry, over three months.

messages.text: With regard to the ruling of the mishna that the animal must be given moist fodder and then dry fodder, a dilemma was raised before the Sages: Does this mean it must be fed moist fodder at the time of moist fodder, i.e., at the end of the rainy season, and dry fodder at the time of dry fodder, at the conclusion of summer? Or perhaps it is fed moist fodder and then dry fodder leftover from the previous summer, both at the time of moist fodder.
messages.quote: ate moist fodder and dry fodder

notes.he: מספוא הגדל באדר וניסן מאכילין אותו באדר וניסן:
notes.en: Moist at the time of moist: fodder that grows in Adar and Nisan, we feed it in Adar and Nisan.

notes.he: מספוא הגדל באלול ותשרי מאכילין אותו בתשרי דלא שחטי ליה עד שיעברו כל ימי הקיץ ויבדק בשניהם:
notes.en: And dry at the time of dry: fodder that grows in Elul and Tishrei, we feed it in Tishrei, for they do not slaughter it until all the days of summer have passed, and it is tested with both.

messages.text: Come and hear, as Rav Idi bar Avin says that Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashiyan said:
The months of Adar and Nisan are the period of moist fodder; Elul and Tishrei are the period of dry fodder.

notes.he: דבההוא זמן הוי יבש תבן וחציר:
notes.en: Elul and Tishrei, dry: for at that time straw and hay are dry.

messages.text: This indicates that the animal is given the fodder that is available at that time.

notes.he: דלח בזמן לח ויבש בזמן יבש:
notes.en: Come and hear: that it is moist at the time of moist and dry at the time of dry.

messages.text: That statement is not necessarily referring to the time when it is fed, as perhaps one feeds it the produce of Elul and Tishrei in Adar and Nisan.
messages.quote: Elul and Tishrei are the period of dry fodder

notes.he: מיהא ליכא למישמע דדלמא ההיא דקאמר אלול ותשרי יבש כלומר דפירות יבשין דאלול ותשרי מאכילין ליה באדר וניסן:
notes.en: From this, at any rate, nothing can be learned, for perhaps what he says, “Elul and Tishrei, dry,” means that we feed it the dry produce of Elul and Tishrei in Adar and Nisan.

messages.text: And how much does one feed it?

notes.he: בכל יום:
notes.en: And how much does one feed it: each day.

messages.text: One feeds it the amount of a fig-bulk.

notes.he: מן הלח ומן היבש אפי' בגרוגרת מכל אחד דיי לבדיקה:
notes.en: And how much does one feed it? Of the moist and of the dry, even a dried fig’s worth of each is enough for the test.

messages.text: They raise a dilemma in the West, Eretz Yisrael: Does this mean that it is fed the amount of a fig-bulk at its first meal each day,

notes.he: שאוכל בכל יום יהבינן לי' מן הרפואה כגרוגרות:
notes.en: At the first meal: that it eats each day, we give it a dried fig’s worth of the remedy.

messages.text: The dilemma from the West that Rava reports continues on 39a: or a fig-bulk at each and every meal?
